newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Buoyant bourse hikes Labouchere profits.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant bourse hikes Labouchere profits.

text.p: Bank Labouchere, a fully-owned banking unit of Dutch insurer Aegon, said on Wednesday 1996 earnings almost doubled, thanks to a buoyant stock market and strong growth in retail investment services.
"We are very happy with the result," chairman Jos Streppel told a results news conference. "It is less than 100 percent profit growth but not far off."
Bank Labouchere earlier reported 1996 earnings mushroomed to 37.68 million guilders from a year-earlier 19.05 million.
"This result also reflects a 4.5 million guilder provision for the costs of the introducing the Euro and (computer software adjustments ahead of) the millennium," Streppel said.
However this was more than offset by a 8.2 million guilder book profit on the sale of money broker Wallich & Matthes. Net after-tax extraordinaries amounted to a gain of 5.32 million.
Streppel said all four of the bank's business units had contributed to the growth in earnings.
Fastest profit grower was retail investment services, thanks in part to a string of recently launched user-friendly products for private investors and growth in client advisory services.
Streppel said Labouchere's Legio Lease direct sales unit had doubled the number of clients for its low-threshold investment products to around 60,000.
One of the most popular products was the "profit doubler", a tax-friendly package of shares and call options.
Labouchere's private banking activities had also grown substantially, with capital under management doubling to four billion guilders from two billion, he said.
In investment banking, Labouchere had become a more active player, acting as counterparty in professional transactions. This had attracted more institutional clients, Streppel said.
Operational services bolstered its market position in clearing and settlement, while the portfolio of securities in custody rose to over 35 billion from 28 billion in 1995.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
